findings.summary: Crash-directory snapshot throws on this machine's dangling crash junction, after deployment and before launch.
findings.failureScenario: C:\ProgramData\Mount and Blade II Bannerlord\crashes is a Junction whose target (Steam workshop item 3717685432 'cache') no longer exists. Test-Path is True, so line 231 runs Get-ChildItem, which throws DirectoryNotFoundException under ErrorActionPreference=Stop. A live -Execute deploys all three private files into the shared module folder (197-223), writes the request, then fails at 231; finally restores and writes status failed with gameLaunched false. The live run cannot succeed. Preflight passes, so nothing warns the operator, and no inert test covers a reparse-point or unreadable crash directory. If the target is ever re-created, the check would watch a Steam-managed workshop folder that Steam may change mid-run, causing false failures.
findings.suggestedFix: In preflight, before any deployment, resolve the crash path and refuse with a clear message if it is a reparse point or cannot be enumerated (or treat it explicitly as 'crash dir unavailable' and record that, if the operator accepts weaker crash evidence). Add an inert scenario for it. Whether to remove or repair the junction is the user's decision; it may belong to another tool or agent.

findings.summary: Inert tests write mock 'passed' receipts into the same runs directory a live run uses.
findings.failureScenario: The runner always writes to build/element-probe-host-v2/runs/<guid>/runtime-receipt.json. Each suite run adds 4 such receipts; there are now 12 (8 before the reviewer's re-run) with status passed-private-native-probe-and-verified-shutdown, gameLaunched true and verifiedShutdownProtocol true (mock PID 78787, fake profile hash, launcherSource = test script). Any later step that globs the runs directory for a passing receipt, or picks the newest one, can take a mock receipt for the live result. Only profileSha256/launcherSource/pid tell them apart.
findings.suggestedFix: Let the test pass a separate run root, or have the runner mark receipts produced with an overridden launcher as inert (a distinct status, never passed). Consumers should require profileSha256 == the reviewed hash and launcherSource == the runner path.

findings.summary: The test seam is live in -Execute: a caller-scope Start-ArmedGame (and any shadowing Get-Process, Copy-Item, Get-CimInstance, Stop-Process or Start-Sleep function) is used silently.
findings.failureScenario: If -Execute is invoked from a session or parent script that defines Start-ArmedGame (or Get-Process), the runner uses it. That can skip the foreign-session check or launch something other than the pinned Bannerlord.exe, and the receipt can still say passed. launcherSource records the override's file (or null when defined interactively), but nothing compares it with the runner's own path. The profile pins the runner's hash, which does not cover caller-scope definitions.
findings.suggestedFix: In -Execute, require (Get-Command Start-ArmedGame).ScriptBlock.File -eq $PSCommandPath and that Get-Process/Copy-Item/Remove-Item/Stop-Process/Get-CimInstance resolve to CmdletInfo. Otherwise force an inert status, or refuse to run.

findings.summary: WaitForExit() after Kill() has no timeout, and the owned watchdog (attached as a debugger) is handled only after the game has exited.
findings.failureScenario: On a hung owned game (timeout path), CloseMainWindow, then Kill, then $owned.WaitForExit() can block forever if termination does not complete while the watchdog debugger is attached. This repo's memory records a hung Bannerlord that Stop-Process did not end but 'taskkill /F /T' did. The runner would then never stop the watchdog, never restore the module files and never release native-test.lock; the shared install keeps the deployed private module. Mechanism unconfirmed for this build; the unbounded wait itself is confirmed in code.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a bounded WaitForExit. If the game is still alive, stop the recorded owned watchdog instance (after re-identifying it), then wait again, bounded. Record the result and continue to restore/receipt in every case.

findings.summary: Owned-watchdog Stop-Process acts by PID after a separate WMI identity check (TOCTOU).
findings.failureScenario: If the watchdog exits and its PID is reused between OwnedWatchdogAlive and Stop-Process, a foreign process could be stopped. The window is very small.
findings.suggestedFix: Get a Process object once, verify StartTime/path on that object, then Kill() through its handle.

findings.summary: A missing rgl_log_errors_<pid>.txt is accepted silently, and the error log is not checked for staleness.
findings.failureScenario: Every real run creates this file. If it is absent (redirected or virtualized logs) the check is skipped, and errorLog is null on a passing receipt. If a stale same-PID file exists, a clean old header satisfies the check.
findings.suggestedFix: Require the file and require LastWriteTimeUtc >= launch, or record errorLogVerified=false and do not pass.

findings.summary: DeclineSafeMode is called for recorded watchdog PIDs without re-checking that the same instance is alive.
findings.failureScenario: If an owned watchdog exits while the game lives and its PID is reused by another process showing a 'Safe Mode' #32770 dialog, that dialog would get 'No'. Practically remote.

findings.summary: The request (10-minute validity in ProbeRequest) is created before the final unbounded FreshWindow wait.
findings.failureScenario: If a foreign session starts just before the launch check and runs for more than about 10 minutes, the host finds a stale request, stays inert, and the runner times out and force-kills its own game. That wastes the launch; it is safe. Inherited from v1.
findings.suggestedFix: Create or refresh the request after the last FreshWindow.

findings.summary: LogRoot (and the crash path derived from it) is a free parameter, and neither is recorded in the receipt.
findings.failureScenario: A non-default LogRoot changes which logs and crash directory the verification uses, and the receipt does not say so.
findings.suggestedFix: Record logPath and crashPath in the receipt; in -Execute, require the default or pin it in the profile.

findings.summary: The real-log replay depends on C:\ProgramData\...\logs\watchdog_log_21268.txt, which is not pinned or retained in the repo.
findings.failureScenario: Only the most recent run's watchdog log survives today (runs 556, 2092, 26872, 30368 and 37192 have rgl logs but no watchdog log). Uncertain: the next game start may delete it. If so, the inert suite throws at line 16 after the live run and can no longer be re-run.
findings.suggestedFix: Copy the real logs into a hashed repo fixture and replay from there.

findings.summary: Restore removes deployed files but not the directories it created. Directory creation is not immediately preceded by a fresh check.
findings.failureScenario: On a clean install, an empty Modules/MNBL.AgentGrowthProbe/bin/Win64_Shipping_Client tree stays behind. It already exists on this machine, so there is no change today.
findings.suggestedFix: Record created directories and remove them if empty during restore.

findings.summary: For exit 0, verifiedShutdownProtocol is also true (kind process-exit-zero).
findings.failureScenario: A consumer that reads verifiedShutdownProtocol=true as 'the watchdog kp protocol was observed' is wrong for exit-0 runs. shutdownVerification.kind tells them apart. No false pass.
findings.suggestedFix: Document this, or add a separate watchdogProtocolVerified flag.

missingTestScenarios: Crash directory that is a reparse point, dangling or unreadable (would have caught B1).
A foreign Watchdog-only process (no Bannerlord*) blocking deploy, launch and restore. The mock only returns 'Bannerlord.Native'.
An owned game that does not exit after Kill (unbounded WaitForExit, S3).
A reused watchdog PID with a different CreationDate: it must count as not alive and must not be stopped.
-Execute with an overridden Start-ArmedGame or a shadowed cmdlet: it must refuse or be marked inert (S2).
Missing or stale rgl_log_errors file (N2); exit-0 runs with crash or error-log entries.
Safe Mode dialog handling (acknowledged as untested in the test receipt's limitations).
limitations: Static and offline only. No game launch, deployment, process start/stop/attach, or -Execute. The runner was run once with -PreflightOnly (read-only).

The contract cross-check proves the 13 decoded spans are byte-identical to the frozen historical contract. Their semantic interpretation (kp emitter, watchdog Process.Kill -> TerminateProcess(-1)) is inherited from that prior review, not re-derived here.

The exit-zero and watchdog-kp paths were exercised only through the inert mocks and the real PID 21268 log replay. The live watchdog parent PID, watchdog exit latency (the runner allows 30 s), first-chance-exception logging by the watchdog during the native probe, and the Safe Mode click were not observed.
S3's hang mechanism (TerminateProcess on a debugged process) is inferred from this repo's memory notes, not reproduced.
N6's log-deletion behaviour is inferred from which logs exist, not confirmed.

The reviewer's inert-test re-run overwrote evidence/engine-extension/managed-element-runner-v2-offline-tests.json (new hash recorded above) and added a fixture suite under build/element-probe-host-v2/inert-runner-tests/ and 29 mock run folders under build/element-probe-host-v2/runs/.
